text:
Maya Lin: Quick sync thread for FinTrust air-gapped POC. They want an audited, repeatable deliverable for on-prem VMs: options for packaging (RPMs vs immutable A/B rootfs vs tarball), offline activation, upgrade cadence, SBOM requirements, and cost estimate including courier. Can we propose a safe default?
Julian Park: Default I'd offer an immutable A/B rootfs image + small delta overlay (overlayfs patch) instead of RPMs. A/B gives atomic switch + rollback path without complex package dependency resolution. Tarball + systemctl scripts works but is more fragile for rollback.
Tess Morales: For smaller deltas we can ship binary diffs produced by bsdiff/xdelta for model-server binaries and layer diffs for rootfs. That keeps update size down — important when courier bandwidth is constrained. Note: model weights often >20GB; we should surface a separate weight shipping plan (separate signed weight artifact).
Ethan (Sales): They asked about SBOM and compliance: need full SBOM for binaries and model metadata, and proof of signature chain. Also will want FIPS-validated components callout.
Julian Park: We can provide SPDX v2.2 SBOM for OS + app + model metadata (model hash, tokenization code version). Signature chain: sign SBOM + bundle with an attestation envelope (RFC 7515-like JSON sig). Example verify command to give them:
```
# verify envelope
curl -sS https://verify.redwood.ai/pubkey.pem | gpg --import -
gpg --verify bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
# check SBOM hash
sha256sum -c bundle.sbom.sha256
```
Tess Morales: Offline activation options: 1) license file with time-bound license key + offline activation token (QR or file), 2) HSM-based signing where customer provides public key, we return attestation, 3) ephemeral operator token that must be applied within 24h. For highest security recommend HSM + customer-managed keys.
Maya Lin: Upgrade cadence for POC — they wanted minimal friction but realistic ops. Suggest: initial full image, then up to 2 deltas during a 6-week POC (security delta at week 2, functional delta at week 4). If they request weekly deltas explain increased test burden.
Ethan (Sales): Pricing ask: offline POC (1 env, 3 hosts) + artifact build + 2 SE days remote + courier + SBOM + legal addendum. Ballpark top-level number?
Tess Morales: Rough estimate: engineering & validation = 2 SE days (build + test) + 2 SRE days (validation + rollback playbook) = ~4 days. Packaging, SBOM, signing automation = 1 eng day. Courier+media ~ $1k-$3k depending on weight/distance. Licensing for POC = $8k-$12k. Total ballpark $13k-$20k. If weights require physical HDD courier can push to $6k+.
Julian Park: Rollback notes: A/B rootfs allows instant rollback by bootloader flag switch, but DB migrations are the usual blocker. For any migration we should supply a migration-guard script that checks a safe-rollback path or makes migrations idempotent. If migrations are irreversible then rollback is not safe -> we must do canary stage and snapshot DB beforehand.
Maya Lin: Constraints to highlight to customer: no live internet for license checks, so all telemetry disabled; offline health checks require local syslog + tar upload via courier if they want logs reviewed; models over 10GB may need separate media. Also call out export-control risk for certain model weights (legal to confirm).
Legal-Bot: Flagging contract items: add media custody clause, data handling and destruction obligations, export-control indemnity language, and EULA addendum for offline activations. Also confirm whether we ship any third-party licensed binaries that require redistribution rights or additional fees.
Ethan (Sales): Next steps: I'll send a short proposal with the 6-week POC plan + pricing range and the A/B image approach. Maya, can you attach a short sample SBOM and the overlay delta example?
Maya Lin: Yes — I'll produce sample SPDX SBOM, sample overlay diff, and a README with verification steps by EOD tomorrow.
Tess Morales: I'll prepare a short rollback playbook and a one-page hardware/media checklist (recommended USB/HDD formatting, checksums, tamper-evident seals).
Julian Park: I'll add a minimal HSM flow doc showing how we'd accept a customer public key and produce an attestation signature.
Ethan (Sales): Great — I'll schedule a 30m review with FinTrust infra/security for Thursday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
